wave_title: The prior generation fixed a real bug in concurrency.rs: Spawn detection checked Expr::Call but not Expr::MethodCall, despite the module's own doc comment already claiming both were covered. This generation generalizes the check beyond that one exact doc-comment phrasing ('function or method') to the underlying STRUCTURAL question -- Call/MethodCall asymmetry -- across every remaining walker, to confirm the fix wasn't a one-off patch over a wider, unexamined pattern.

findings.result: SYMMETRIC BY DESIGN, ALREADY VERIFIED -- neither Call nor MethodCall attempts any spelling-based classification at all; OWNERSHIP only cares about bare-identifier value positions and &/&mut sites, both orthogonal to call shape. No asymmetry possible here since neither arm does spelling-based work.

ALREADY SYMMETRIC -- Expr::Call checks persistence_candidate_kind(&call.func) (a free/path spelling); Expr::MethodCall checks persistence_kind_for_spelling(&method_call.method.to_string()) (a bare method-name spelling) using the SAME shared closed spelling set (persistence_kind_for_spelling), explicitly factored out for exactly this reason per its own doc comment ('the SAME recognizer ... factored out to guarantee the two ... cannot silently drift apart', originally written for a different pair of walkers but the same discipline applies here to Call vs MethodCall). No gap found -- this was the correct reference example the CONCURRENCY fix should (and now does) match.

ASYMMETRIC, BUT DELIBERATE AND ALREADY DOCUMENTED -- Expr::Call checks effect_kind_for_free_call_spelling (fs/File/Command/TcpStream/TcpListener/UnixStream/UnixListener qualifiers); Expr::MethodCall performs no check at all. This asymmetry has an explicit, principled, already-recorded reason (this session's own prior evidence records): a bare method name carries no qualifying module/type, making it far more likely to collide with an unrelated type's own identically-named method, unlike a free/path call's explicit qualifier. Confirmed this reasoning is sound and was actually applied consistently (not merely asserted) by re-reading the module's own doc comment and the three prior evidence records that established it.

SYMMETRIC BY DESIGN -- CALL's own declared purpose is to record every call site regardless of shape; Expr::Call and Expr::MethodCall are explicitly grouped together (`syn::Expr::Call(_) | syn::Expr::MethodCall(_)`) at the two call sites that matter for its own bespoke logic (visibility-boundary tracking and dispatch-kind determination), confirming they are already treated as one shared case, not two independently-maintained ones.
FIXED LAST GENERATION -- the one real asymmetry found this sweep, already closed.
